title: Teaching children (Deuteronomy 6:7)
hook: teach them diligently, at home and on the way
tomorrow: teach a grandchild, says the Talmud, and it's as if what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Friday night blessing: Ephraim and Manasseh, the four mothers, the priests' words. Hands on heads. Today, what the hands do the rest of the week.
screen: `HANDS ON HEADS.` → `THE REST OF THE WEEK.`

segments.voice: Kids ask the biggest questions at the worst moments: from the back seat, in the bath, halfway out the door with one shoe on. Why do people die? Is God real? Where was I before I was born? Nobody schedules those. A verse in Deuteronomy seems to have known that already.
screen: `FROM THE BACK SEAT.` → `IS GOD REAL? ONE SHOE ON.` → `NOBODY SCHEDULES THOSE.`

segments.voice: It's in the Shema, and the JPS translation reads: "and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up." Look where the teaching happens. Not at a desk. At home, on a walk, at bedtime, at breakfast. The teaching rides along with ordinary life. The Hebrew for teach them diligently is v'shinantam, and Rashi reads it this way: let the words be sharp in your mouth, so that when someone asks, you don't stammer, you answer. Short, clear, ready. The Talmud, in Kiddushin, lists what a father owes his son, and it's practical: teach him Torah, teach him a trade, and some say, teach him to swim. Teaching for a whole life, not only for a test. None of it requires a parent with every answer. Here's a sentence a parent could say at dinner: that's a big question; here's what our tradition says, here's what I still wonder, let's look it up together. That's teaching on the way.
screen: `AT HOME, ON THE WAY, AT BEDTIME.` · `SHARP IN YOUR MOUTH: NO STAMMER.` · `TORAH, A TRADE, AND SWIMMING.` · `WHAT WE SAY, WHAT I WONDER.` · then, large: `TEACH THEM DILIGENTLY.`

segments.voice: Choose one thing you know well enough to teach a child: a blessing, a story, how to tie a knot, how to say sorry. Say it out loud in one plain sentence, as if a kid had just asked from the back seat. Then say it once more, shorter and sharper.
screen: `ONE THING YOU KNOW.` · `SAY IT OUT LOUD, PLAINLY.` · `NOW SHORTER, SHARPER.`

segments.voice: Teaching children: diligently, at home and on the way, at bedtime and at breakfast. Sharp in your mouth, ready when they ask.

howItsDone: Deuteronomy 6:7 is part of the Shema, said morning and evening; Jewish parents teach at home through Shabbat and holidays, bedtime Shema and questions at the table, alongside Hebrew school or day school.
